cases.counterfactual_program:
(rule! (lambda (g)
         (let* ((h (rows g))
                (w (cols g)))
           (let* ((order (reduce (lambda (acc rc)
                                   (let* ((r (/ rc w))
                                          (c (mod rc w))
                                          (v (at g r c)))
                                     (if (and
                                           (> v 0)
                                           (not (find (lambda (x) (= x v)) acc)))
                                         (append acc (list v))
                                         acc)))
                                 (list)
                                 (range 0 (* h w))))
                  (first-cells (reduce (lambda (acc rc)
                                         (let* ((r (/ rc w))
                                                (c (mod rc w))
                                                (v (at g r c)))
                                           (if (and
                                                 (> v 0)
                                                 (not (find (lambda (x) (= (first x) v))
                                                            acc)))
                                               (append acc (list (list v r c)))
                                               acc)))
                                       (list)
                                       (range 0 (* h w))))
                  (rs (map second first-cells))
                  (cs (map third first-cells))
                  (row-span (- (max-list rs) (min-list rs)))
                  (col-span (- (max-list cs) (min-list cs)))
                  (n (length order)))
             (if (>= row-span col-span)
                 (build-grid n 1 (r c) (nth order r))
                 (build-grid 1 n (r c) (nth order c)))))))

step_a: scan row-major and record ordered first-hit color/coordinate triples
step_b: compare coordinate spans, orient the output, and place colors in the episode order
why_b_depends_on_a: the first-hit triples determine both the row/column orientation and the color sequence consumed by the output-order setting
